entries.title: Mulgore
body: A sheltered, pastoral valley of green grass and mesas in the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, walled in by mountains on every side and reached only through a pass in the south-east. It is the ancestral home of the tauren, and the tall cliffs of their capital, Thunder Bluff, rise over its fields.

For hundreds of years the tauren had no land of their own. Hunted by the centaurs, they wandered the harsh Barrens as nomads, until Thrall's orcs helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive the centaurs from Mulgore. Now its plains are full of game and its people are at peace, though not without trouble: quilboar, harpies, gnolls, goblin prospectors and dwarven diggers all press on the edges of the valley.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Mulgore (introduction, History, World of Warcraft, Geography)

entries.title: Red Cloud Mesa
body: The rolling plains atop the high cliffs of southern Mulgore, once a place of peaceful, serene beauty. The Bristleback quilboar have laid siege to it, spreading out of their ravine and growing twisted, thorny vines over every piece of land they take. Burned tauren huts mark the front line, and the mesa's water well has been destroyed.

entries.title: Camp Narache
body: The main village of the Hawkwind tribe, on the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa, and the camp where young tauren begin their training. Wounded braves rest in its great tent, and its trainers gather in a circle at its centre to honour their fallen matriarch, Greatmother Hawkwind.

entries.title: Brambleblade Ravine
body: The home of the Bristleback quilboar on the north-eastern edge of Red Cloud Mesa. Their leader, Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, keeps a great hut at the back of the ravine, and from here the quilboar push out across the mesa.

entries.title: Bloodhoof Village
body: A tauren village in central Mulgore, named for the Bloodhoof tribe and surrounded on three sides by the waters of Stonebull Lake. It is where wild kodo are tamed for riding, and where young tauren come after leaving Camp Narache.
Baine Bloodhoof, son of the High Chieftain, leads the village and sees to its protection, and Zarlman Two-Moons cares for the spiritual needs of the tribe.

entries.title: The Water Wells
body: Three sacred wells across Mulgore supply the tauren with water: the Winterhoof at the edge of the Rolling Plains, the Thunderhorn on the road to Thunder Bluff, and the Wildmane, northernmost of all, just beyond the city.
The Venture Company seized and poisoned them to control the valley's water. Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village leads the effort to cleanse them.

entries.title: Stonebull Lake
body: A long horseshoe-shaped lake around Bloodhoof Village, known for its abundant fish. A bridge spans it at its narrowest point, carrying the road to Thunder Bluff.

On its north-eastern shore a Venture Company caravan carrying mining supplies was caught by tauren outrunners and burned. Its smoking remains still sit on a mound, defended by the goblins who came back to salvage them.

entries.title: The Venture Co. Mine
body: An enormous mine in the eastern cliffs of Mulgore, run by Supervisor Fizsprocket. The tauren refused the Venture Company mining rights in their homeland, and the goblins would not take no for an answer.
Their board, under Mogul Razdunk, has urged Fizsprocket to expand into logging too, and promised him new shredders and materials for a lumber mill.

entries.title: Bael'dun Digsite
body: A great quarry cut into the mountains on Mulgore's western edge by dwarves of the expedition at Bael Modan. Baine Bloodhoof warned them that their digging was an affront to the Earth Mother.
The dwarves refused to listen, and when talking failed, the Bloodhoof resolved to drive them out by taking and breaking their picks.

entries.title: Palemane Rock
body: A cave in western Mulgore that runs deep into the mountainside, home of the Palemane gnolls. They live inside it and in a camp outside, and in scattered camps along the southern mountains, and attack anyone who comes too close.

entries.title: Windfury Ridge
body: The far northern reaches of Mulgore, claimed by the Windfury harpies. They swoop down to capture or kill anyone who comes near their nests. The tauren hunt them for their brilliant feathers, which decorate weddings and feasts in Thunder Bluff.

entries.title: Red Rocks
body: A formation of red sandstone in north-eastern Mulgore, the sacred burial ground of the tauren tribes. Here fallen heroes are sent to the Earth Mother and the Sky Father by cleansing flame. Only the most valiant are laid to rest here: the warriors who helped found and defend Thunder Bluff, and those who gave their lives for their tribes.

Red Rocks is a place of life's great journeys too. Young braves come to fulfil their rites of adulthood, listening for the wisdom of their ancestors on the wind. Lately Bristleback quilboar have invaded and defiled it, to the fury of Thunder Bluff.

entries.title: The Golden Plains
body: The Golden Plains around Thunder Bluff are among the most treasured parts of the tauren homeland and their favourite hunting grounds. Great herds of kodo gather there, and it is said the famous Arra'chea roams the shifting sea of grass.

The Rolling Plains cover the south from Bloodhoof Village to the Barrens. Wolves, kodo, tallstriders and cougars live there, and it is the only part of Mulgore centaur outriders still manage to reach.

entries.title: Cairne Bloodhoof
body: High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes and chieftain of the Bloodhoof. He grew up near the shores of the Great Sea in the Barrens, a childhood friend of Hamuul Runetotem. His lifemate Tamaala bore him a son, Baine, and died before the Third War.

A peerless warrior and a wise leader, slowed somewhat by age but still strong, Cairne never gave up hope of leading his people to a land where they could live in peace. When the centaurs threatened to wipe them out, he found that hope in Thrall's orcs, and in Mulgore. He is one of the Horde's most venerated leaders.

entries.title: Baine Bloodhoof
body: The son of Cairne Bloodhoof, who leads Bloodhoof Village. During the founding of the new Horde, centaurs captured him and threw his father into despair, until the half-ogre Rexxar rescued him and brought the tauren back into the Horde. His father hopes one day to hand the leadership of the tauren down to him.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Mulgore (The Third War and after)

entries.title: The Hawkwinds of Narache
body: The family that leads the Hawkwind tribe at Camp Narache. Chief Hawkwind sends promising young tauren out into the world; his mother, Greatmother Hawkwind, is honoured by the trainers who gather in a circle around her.

entries.title: Mull Thunderhorn
body: A tauren of Bloodhoof Village who leads the effort to cleanse Mulgore's poisoned water wells, making totems to purify the waters the Venture Company fouled.

entries.title: Morin Cloudstalker
body: A tauren who keeps watch from his post on the road east of Bloodhoof Village, determined to root out the foothold the Venture Company has established in Mulgore.

entries.title: The Great Hunt
body: The tauren are a peaceful people, but the rites of the Great Hunt are the heart of their spiritual life. Every tauren, warrior or not, seeks an identity both as a hunter and as a child of the Earth Mother.

When young tauren come of age, they must test their skills in the wilds of Mulgore and prove themselves in the Great Hunt. Hunting and shamanism are honoured above most things in their culture, together with their respect for the land and nature.

entries.title: The Tauren Come to Mulgore
body: For countless generations the centaurs harried the tauren, forcing them into a nomadic life in the Barrens and hunting the game they lived on nearly to extinction. When Thrall's orcs landed in Kalimdor, the tauren saw kindred spirits in them, with honour and strength, and looked to them for protection.

With the orcs' help, Cairne's Bloodhoof tribe drove the centaurs back and claimed the grasslands of Mulgore. For the first time in hundreds of years the tauren had a land of their own. Cairne built a refuge on the mesas of Thunder Bluff for every tribe, and one by one the scattered tribes united under him.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Mulgore (The Third War and after, World of Warcraft)

entries.title: The Grimtotem
body: Not every tribe agrees on the path the tauren nation should take. The Grimtotem, one of the mightiest tribes, are the aggressive extreme of a peaceful people. They want to wipe the "lesser races" from Kalimdor and take back the tauren's lost lands, and almost every other race is their enemy.

While other tauren children learn the rites of the Great Hunt, Grimtotem children are taught to fight. Their leader is the shaman Magatha Grimtotem, who took power after her husband died in an "unforeseen climbing accident", and who sits among the elders of Thunder Bluff.
